steps.title: Axes
steps.instruction: Trace the two axes of the graph.

note.text: The side axis shows temperature in degrees Celsius. The bottom axis shows the days of the week.
note.remember: Read across the bottom, up the side.

steps.title: Scale marks
steps.instruction: Draw the tick marks at 10, 20 and 30 degrees.

note.text: Evenly spaced marks make a scale, so every degree takes up the same height on the graph.

steps.title: Bars
steps.instruction: Draw a bar for each day, as tall as that day's temperature.

note.text: Each bar's height shows the temperature from the table at the top. Comparing bars shows patterns at a glance.

options.feedback: Yes. Thursday's bar is the tallest, at 24 degrees.
Monday's bar is the shortest, so it was the coolest day.
Wednesday was warm at 21 degrees, but Thursday's bar is taller.
Friday cooled down to 18 degrees. Look for the tallest bar.

steps.title: Find the pattern
steps.instruction: Look at how the bars change.
steps.question: What pattern does the graph show this week?

options.text: It got warmer each day until Thursday, then cooled on Friday
options.feedback: Right. Graphs make patterns easy to spot. Weather data over many weeks shows what each season is usually like.
The bars have different heights, so the temperatures changed.
The bars get taller from Monday to Thursday, so it got warmer.
Friday's bar is shorter than Thursday's.
